description:
During the read_primitives cross-surface burn-down (PR #891) three Polars
platform helpers were found buggy and FIXED at the source with regression tests
(PR #891, commit "fix(dataframe): repair window_lag/lead/ntile + UnifiedExpr.desc()
sort marker"; tests in tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_window_and_sort_fixes.py):
  - window_lag / window_lead (polars_df.py): now shift in the window ORDER BY
    order via shift().over(partition, order_by=...).
  - window_ntile (polars_df.py): now uses the correct SQL NTILE piecewise bucket
    formula.
  - UnifiedExpr.desc() (unified_frame.py): now a real descending sort marker.

Because the helpers were buggy at the time, a few read_primitives EXPRESSION impls
were written with inline raw Polars (via `.native`) to route around them. Those
impls are correct and fully gate-verified, but now that the helpers are fixed they
could be simplified back onto the unified API for readability/portability (the
unified helpers also work on non-Polars expression backends, whereas the inline
`.native` Polars is Polars-only).

Candidate impls (benchbox/core/read_primitives/dataframe_queries.py), all
EXPRESSION-family only (the pandas impls are already idiomatic pandas):
  - window_lead_lag_expression_impl (impl_base of window_lead_lag_same_frame):
    raw pl.col(...).shift(±1).over(...) -> ctx.window_lag / ctx.window_lead.
  - qualify_lag_lead_expression_impl: raw shift(1).over(...) -> ctx.window_lag.
  - qualify_ntile_expression_impl: inline NTILE piecewise -> ctx.window_ntile.

IMPORTANT PREREQUISITE (why this is not a trivial swap): the catalog SQL for
these queries now carries a deterministic window ORDER BY TIE-BREAK
(e.g. `ORDER BY o_orderdate, o_orderkey`, `ORDER BY o_totalprice, o_orderkey`),
and the inline impls sort by that COMPOSITE key. The current helper signatures
take `order_by: list[tuple[str, bool]]` but only read `order_by[0]` (a SINGLE
order column). So before the impls can use the helpers, the helpers must be
extended to honor a MULTI-COLUMN order_by (composite tie-break). Without that,
swapping in the helpers would drop the tie-break and re-introduce the
non-deterministic-window divergences the burn-down fixed.

NOT candidates (these use raw Polars for ops the unified API genuinely lacks -
leave them inline): window_moving_frame (bounded ROWS / 30-day RANGE frames),
statistical_correlation / statistical_variance (population moments: pl.cov,
pl.corr, var/std with ddof), olap_cube_analysis / olap_rollup_analysis (CUBE /
ROLLUP grouping-set unions), timeseries_trend_analysis (regression slope over
epoch seconds). These have no unified-helper equivalent and are out of scope.

This is OPTIONAL cleanup: the inline impls are correct and the gate is green, so
this only reduces Polars-specific code in favor of the portable unified helpers.
Defer indefinitely if the churn is not worth it.

anti_patterns.why: this cleanup is about the Polars expression family only.

anti_patterns.dont: swap impls onto the helpers before w1
anti_patterns.why: the helpers only honor order_by[0] today, so the composite tie-break would be silently dropped and the gate would regress

anti_patterns.dont: touch the unsupported-op impls (rolling frames, ddof moments, CUBE/ROLLUP, regression slope)
anti_patterns.why: the unified API has no equivalent

deferrals.reason: The descending=[...] form is canonical and clearer; now that desc() is fixed both work, but there is no value in churning these back.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Reason explicitly argues against doing this: no value in churning .sort() calls back once both forms work equivalently.

preserves.behavior: The deterministic window tie-breaks (the composite ORDER BY) are preserved - dropping them would re-introduce non-deterministic-window divergences.
The read_primitives cross-surface gate stays green (every compared cell matches; no NEW known_divergences).
pandas impls and the raw-Polars impls for unsupported ops (window_moving_frame, statistical_correlation/variance, olap_cube/rollup, timeseries_trend_analysis) are left as-is.

prior_art.concept: benchbox/core/read_primitives/dataframe_queries.py:window_lead_lag_expression_impl/qualify_lag_lead_expression_impl/qualify_ntile_expression_impl — the inline raw-Polars impls to simplify (expression family only).
benchbox/platforms/dataframe/polars_df.py:window_lag — currently does `order_by[0]` only; the single-key limitation is the blocker for the tie-break queries.
benchbox/platforms/dataframe/polars_df.py:window_lag/window_lead/window_ntile — the fixed helpers to extend with multi-column order_by, then call from the impls.
tests/integration/test_read_primitives_cross_surface_equivalence.py — the gate test that must stay green after the refactor (the real safety net).
tests/unit/platforms/dataframe/test_window_and_sort_fixes.py — extend with multi-column order_by assertions before relying on it in the impls.

verifications.expected: tests pass, including new multi-column order_by cases

verifications.description: read_primitives gate still green after the refactor
verifications.expected: exit 0; 'SQL and DataFrame surfaces are equivalent (modulo classified exceptions)'

work_units.notes:
Generalize the helpers from `order_by[0]` to the full `order_by` list:
shift().over(partition, order_by=[cols...], descending=[...]) for lag/lead, and
rank('ordinal') over the composite order for ntile. Add unit-test cases with a
two-column order_by (a value column + an id tie-break) to
test_window_and_sort_fixes.py.
work_units.summary: Extend window_lag/window_lead/window_ntile to honor a multi-column order_by (composite tie-break), with unit tests

work_units.notes:
Replace the inline raw-Polars in window_lead_lag_expression_impl,
qualify_lag_lead_expression_impl, qualify_ntile_expression_impl with
ctx.window_lag / ctx.window_lead / ctx.window_ntile using the composite
order_by (matching the catalog SQL tie-break). Leave the pandas impls and the
genuinely-unsupported-op impls (window_moving_frame, statistical_*, olap_*,
timeseries) untouched.
